Lessons.Title: Graphs of Exponential Functions
ExplanationParagraphs: Exponential graphs f(x)=a·b^x have domain all real values and, when a>0, strictly positive outputs; their horizontal asymptote is y=0.
For f(x)=a·b^(x−h)+k, horizontal translation h and vertical translation k move the asymptote to y=k. A negative a reflects across the horizontal baseline.
Reflection across the y-axis replaces x by −x; f(−x) changes growth direction without changing the y-intercept.
A vertical scale factor multiplies the distances of curve points from their baseline; use transformed anchor points and explicit range/domain.
To estimate solutions of a b^x+d=c graphically, locate curve/line intersection, then refine numerically to the required precision.
Independent Cool-down: (1) Graph g(x)=2^(x−1)−3 and give domain/range/asymptote. (2) Reflect f(x)=3^x about y-axis. (3) Estimate 2^x=6 from graphical reasoning.
Independent Try It 1: Compare y=4^x and y=(1/4)^x at x=−1,0,1.
Independent Try It 2: Graph h(x)=3^(x−1)−2 and give asymptote and range.
Independent Try It 3: Approximate x where 3^x=7.
Independent Try It 4: Give formula and intercept for stretching y=(1/2)^x by factor 5.
Independent Try It 5: Reflect y=3^x about the x-axis and identify range.
Independent Try It 6: Reflect y=2^x across y-axis then shift up1.

WorkedExamples.Title: Graph exponential growth and decay
WorkedExamples.Question: Graph f(x)=3^x and g(x)=(1/3)^x for x=-2,-1,0,1,2.
WorkedExamples.Method: Transform model graph and check asymptote, domain, range and intercepts.
Steps: For f use 1/9,1/3,1,3,9; g uses 9,3,1,1/3,1/9. Both have domain R, range positive, horizontal y=0; reflection across y-axis.
WorkedExamples.Answer: For f use 1/9,1/3,1,3,9; g uses 9,3,1,1/3,1/9. Both have domain R, range positive, horizontal y=0; reflection across y-axis.
WorkedExamples.Check: Calculate plotted anchor values and check transformation direction.

WorkedExamples.Question: Graph g(x)=2^(x−2)+3 from parent f(x)=2^x.

Steps: Shift right 2 and up 3, horizontal y=3; domain R, range (3,∞), y-intercept (0,13/4).
WorkedExamples.Answer: Shift right 2 and up 3, horizontal y=3; domain R, range (3,∞), y-intercept (0,13/4).

Steps: Every y-value is multiplied by3; y-intercept (0,3); horizontal y=0; domain R, range (0,∞).

KeyConcepts.Title: Parent exponential graph
KeyConcepts.Rule: Domain R, range (0,∞), y-intercept 1, horizontal asymptote 0.

KeyConcepts.Title: Horizontal/vertical shift
KeyConcepts.Definition: g(x)=a b^(x−h)+k shifts parent curve by (h,k).
KeyConcepts.Rule: Horizontal asymptote is y=k; sign a sets above/below.

KeyConcepts.Title: Reflections
KeyConcepts.Definition: f(−x) reflects across y-axis and −f(x) reflects across x-axis.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Keep careful track of sign placement inside versus outside exponent.

KeyConcepts.Title: Visual numerical approximation
KeyConcepts.Definition: Solve f(x)=c by reading intersection; refine to requested precision.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Graph-only values are approximate and should be checked numerically.

SummaryPoints: Do not mistake horizontal asymptotes for points the curve must cross.
Range shifts depend on sign of vertical multiplier.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Shift right when exponent is x+2.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use x−h for right shift by h.

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The first is reflected positive-base exponential; the second is not real for many noninteger x.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Keep the negative scalar outside the exponential.
